Reviewer verdict: **Ready for the maintainer to merge** (one documentation-only request before merge)

## What looks good

- The order and link stages are faithful ports with their named reasons: the chain order (`chain.rs`, `air_chain::chains`), the back-along chord (`air_chain::link`) and the edge route (`ring_links::edge_route`) all carry their own doc comments and provenance lines.
- The marks go with their curves: `OrderedSet::new` moves each named stretch to the index of its curve in the ordered set (reversed stretches in the new direction), and the law suite pins the count and placement — no planner can drop or move a mark.
- The negative pins are the right ones: a link across the island is refused with the part reason, a lift with no reason is refused, and an order that moves a curve is refused. The pins for the lift counts (disc 0, dog bone 0, island 7/7/5) are measured against the pinned law suite and the motion `kernel_laws` readings.
- Law L3 ("the start side changes only the order and the start point") holds with the kernel planner set, and the motion `kernel_laws` k4 test pins 0 lifts and 0 crossings on the disc and the dog bone — better than the old 2D Pocket (18/26 lifts, none named) and the #3934 level blend.

## Results (trial merged with `origin/side/path-kernel`, 25f3838db - "Already up to date", clean)

Local, worktree `.claude/worktrees/cc-pr4234-review`, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6:

- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --lib` : 86 passed (segments unit tests: 7 passed)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test geo2d` : 16 passed
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --lib` : 5 passed (route tests included)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --test laws` : 122 passed
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test kernel_laws` : 29 passed (incl. `kernel_order_and_link_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone`)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` : clean
- `cargo xtask gate light` : 7 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (motion lib 304s, adaptive_troch_island 41s, adaptive_troch_neck 17s, adaptive_troch_parallel 10s, app pocket_pass_start 3s, app offset_pass_start 54s, light build 884s; wall 24.7 min)

No post or toolpath code changed (no old planner touched; the kernel is not called by any planner yet), so no example-catalog suites are owed. This is a P2-class PR under the safety floor for the link proof (the link stage decides where the tool stays down); the link stage is not wired in by any planner yet, so no targeted heavy step is owed at this step — pins are the local suites above.

## Requested before merge (one item, documentation accuracy)

1. `crates/pathkernel/src/link/proof.rs:28-30` - the `AIR` doc comment reads "A centre within this part of the tool radius of the stock edge has half of the tool in the air", which is not what the constant does. `AIR = 0.1` is used as a 0.1 tool-radius band around the stock edge (on either side of it) that counts as open ground, and the old ring links use `AIR * r` as "outside the stock by 0.1 r" (a centre that far out cuts at most 0.9 r into the stock). Either the comment should say that (a centre within 0.1 r of the stock edge counts as air), or the constant and the use should change to the old semantics. The same loose phrasing appears in `docs/decisions/4177-kernel-order-link.md` ("where half of the tool is in the air").

## Questions / notes (non-blocking)

- `AIR` is a broader semantic than the old code's "outside the stock by 0.1 r": the kernel also allows a sample inside the stock within 0.1 r of the edge. That is the named decision ("The edge strip of the stock counts as air") and the disc/dog-bone pins pass, but a narrow band whose outermost ring sits more than 0.9 r from the stock edge and which is not otherwise cleared would pass the UNCUT_STOCK check as open. Worth a pin on a narrow band or an explicit note that the edge strip is assumed to be cleared by a cut.
- `crates/pathkernel/src/order/stage.rs:68-89`, `heavy()`: a `Span::Whole` full-width mark sets `Heavy::Whole` but the pick does not place the curve anywhere special (no end-of-stretch start); only `Span::Part` curves get the "heavy stretch cut last" treatment. The doc comment says "a closed curve starts where its longest full-width stretch ends" without a Whole-span case. Either say so or place the start at the canonical lowest vertex (it is today).
- `crates/pathkernel/src/order/stage.rs:119-124`, `starts()`: a row (`Family::Row`) on the first step (no tool position yet) is pushed as-cut, never reversed (`starts(...)` only reverses a row when `at` is `Some(q)`). Probably deliberate (the row has no direction then), but worth a comment.
- `crates/pathkernel/src/link/proof.rs:217`, `link()`: the `hop.unwrap_or(Hop::Lift(CUTS_PART))` fallback is unreachable today (the lift reasons are all named constants) but silently converts any future refusal into a `CUTS_PART` lift. Named reasons would be safer as an explicit match, not a fallback.
- The order stage recomputes the `planned` cut list (`stage.rs:172-178`) on each pick iteration (O(n^2) overall); fine for the current kernel, worth knowing for large parts.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Reviewer verdict: **Ready for the maintainer to merge** (the needs-rework item is closed; no blockers found)

## What looks good

- The `AIR` constant is removed. Open ground is now only the air of the region or a sample within the swath (0.9 tool radii) of a cut already made. The doc comment of `link/proof.rs` and the decision file state what the code does, including the old meaning of the ring links' `AIR` ("outside the stock by 0.1 r") and why the kernel has no such band (its centre area ends at the stock edge and its air starts one tool radius outside).
- Each lift arm has its own named constant and no fallback: a chord that would cut the part lifts with `CUTS_PART` (or `HITS_FIXTURE` near a keep-out), a touch of a planned cut lifts with `CROSSES_CUT`, stock no cut cleared lifts with `UNCUT_STOCK`, a path with no finite point lifts with `BAD_PATH`, a non-planar region with `NOT_PLANAR_LINK`, and `Retract` lifts with `USER_RETRACT`. The policy match is exhaustive. No `unwrap_or(CUTS_PART)` remains.
- The new pin `a_link_along_the_stock_edge_over_uncut_stock_is_refused` (laws/order_link.rs) pins the edge strip: refused with `UNCUT_STOCK` over the uncut strip along the stock edge, and the same link stays when a made cut clears the strip. This also closes the note from the previous review (a narrow-band pin).
- A curve with a `Span::Whole` full-width mark sits after the other ready curves and starts as a plain curve (no stretch end), named in each match case (order/stage.rs). The pin `a_whole_full_width_curve_is_cut_after_the_other_ready_curves` pins the cut-last rule and the nearest-vertex start.
- A row on the first step never reverses and keeps the guide's own direction (a comment says why); the pin `a_row_on_the_first_step_keeps_its_direction_and_the_next_rows_zigzag` pins the first-row determinism, the zigzag of the next rows, and that the input direction of the rows does not change the first cut.
- The planned list is built once for the walk and each taken cut is removed from it (order/stage.rs, `planned` and `planned_of`).

## Results (trial merge against `origin/side/path-kernel` — "Already up to date", clean)

Local, worktree `.claude/worktrees/cc-pr4234-review`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6`, `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`:

- `cargo check --tests -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-motion`: clean
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --test laws`: 125 passed
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --lib`: 5 passed
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test kernel_laws`: 29 passed (incl. `kernel_order_and_link_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone`)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --lib`: 86 passed (incl. the 7 segments unit tests)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test geo2d`: 16 passed
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- The three review-fix pins by name: all pass

The author's full batch gate on the final head (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel`: 1223 steps, 0 failed, includes clippy, `laws`, `kernel_laws`, and the `example_catalog*` suites) was not re-run here: it is author-gated, and this review is scoped to the fixes. `cargo xtask gate light` was not re-run either: the light twins live in `kernel`, `motion` and `app`, and no light twin reaches the kernel (no planner calls it yet). The earlier 7-step green on the pre-fix head is unaffected by this change.

## Targeted tests

- `order_link::a_link_along_the_stock_edge_over_uncut_stock_is_refused` (pass)
- `order_link::a_whole_full_width_curve_is_cut_after_the_other_ready_curves` (pass)
- `order_link::a_row_on_the_first_step_keeps_its_direction_and_the_next_rows_zigzag` (pass)
- The laws `LIFTS` table pins the lift counts: disc and dog bone 13/15 on Outside (Auto resolves to Outside), 0 on Inside, the pocket with an island 7/7/5 — all named. The motion `kernel_laws` k4 test pins the same (0 crossings, each lift named, tally equal to the lifts).

No post or toolpath code changed (no old planner touched, no planner calls the kernel yet), so no example-catalog suites are owed. This is a safety-floor change for the link proof, but the kernel is not wired into any planner yet, so no targeted heavy step is owed at this step; the pins are the evidence.

## Requested before merge

None. The one item of the previous review (the `AIR` doc line) is closed and verified.

## Questions / notes (non-blocking)

- The bands round a part lift on Outside (13 disc, 15 dog bone): the link from one piece at the stock edge to the next runs over the strip the next piece cuts, and the kernel cannot leave the stock into the air there (its air starts one tool radius outside). The lifts are named and the counts are pinned; follow-up #4241 records the gap.
- The planned list is built once per walk (not once per step); each taken cut is removed from it. It is O(n^2) in total, because each proof rebuilds the lines of the level. A cache for those lines is not in this step.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
